market.domesticSlice: India's PLI/ACC scheme allocates ₹18,100 Cr for 50GWh of domestic advanced-chemistry-cell capacity by 2030. Named India peers: Exide Industries (ROE 7.05%), Amara Raja (ROE 14.0%), Log9 Materials (cautionary — entered NCLT insolvency by Nov 2025 despite $56.1M raised), Livguard ($65.1M raised, financials not found).

structureFacts: India's ACC/PLI scheme is a real, funded government structural tailwind targeting 50GWh domestic capacity by 2030

Cell chemistry itself (cells) is still largely imported from Japan/Korea/China even by India-based pack assemblers with real domestic value-add (BMS, pack assembly, in-house components) — this is a structural industry pattern, not company-specific weakness
Log9 Materials' 2025 NCLT insolvency despite $56.1M raised is a cautionary data point on the segment's capital intensity and execution risk, even for well-funded entrants

adoptionStructure.note: OEM battery qualification requires certification (AIS 156 Amendment III Phase 2, ICAT for NMC/LFP chemistries, TSEC approval for telecom) — these are must-have, not nice-to-have, gates for supplying two-wheeler EV OEMs and telecom infrastructure buyers.
